                         DIRECT TESTIMONY OF NELDA HOWTON
                                I. IDENTIFICATION AND BACKGROUND
Q. Please state your name, address, and occupation.
A. My name is Nelda Howton. I reside at 12600 FM 2843, Salado, Texas 76571. I hold a Bachelor's degree from
Texas A&M; International University and a Master's degree from Baylor University. I have worked as a teacher,
principal, college biotechnology director, and educational consultant. I currently work with Educate Texas in
collaboration with the Texas Education Agency supporting P-TECH and Early College High School leadership
initiatives.

                                        II. NATURE OF TESTIMONY
Q. What is the nature of your testimony?
A. My testimony is based on my personal observations, firsthand knowledge, and experience as a landowner
whose residence, agricultural operations, livestock, water resources, and quality of life would be directly
impacted by the proposed 765-kV transmission line. To the extent I discuss publicly available studies, scientific
materials, governmental publications, or other articles, I do so only to explain the basis of my concerns and
understanding as a layperson and not as expert testimony. See Exhibit 6.

                                       III. PURPOSE OF TESTIMONY
Q. What is the purpose of your testimony?
A. The purpose of my testimony is to oppose all proposed routes utilizing Link F-20, including Route 894, and to
support Route 767 as a preferable alternative because it would reduce concentrated impacts to residences,
agricultural operations, and community resources. The route maps and comparative route materials supporting
my testimony are included as Exhibit 2.

                                        IV. SUMMARY OF POSITION
Q. Please summarize your position.
A. I oppose routes utilizing Link F-20 because those routes place an extraordinary burden on my property and
neighboring landowners. The proposed line would be located approximately 242 feet from the centerline to my
residence and approximately 143 feet from the nearest transmission structures and conductor locations, as
reflected in the aerial proximity exhibit. See Exhibit 3. I am concerned about visual impacts, audible corona
noise, reduced enjoyment and use of my property, potential effects on livestock behavior and agricultural
operations, fire risk in an area already vulnerable to wildfire conditions, and long-term impacts to property value
and future residential use. Property photographs and aerial imagery are included as Exhibit 1. I support Route 767
because it appears to distribute impacts more evenly and avoid concentrated impacts to existing homes and
community features. See Exhibit 2.

                              V. PROPERTY DESCRIPTION AND LAND USE
Q. Please describe your property and its current use.
A. My family owns approximately 47 acres used for cattle production, horse activities, deer hunting, poultry
production, gardening, and general agricultural operations. We maintain barns, fencing, corrals, and a residence
on the property. The property has historically supported Hereford cattle and other livestock operations. The land
is also used by family members and visiting children and grandchildren for outdoor activities and recreational
use. The general property layout is shown in Exhibit 1, and examples of active livestock, equine, and poultry uses
are shown in Exhibits 5.1 through 5.3.

                                VI. IMPACTS OF THE PROPOSED ROUTE


                                       Direct Testimony of Nelda Howton - Page 1
 Q. What impacts do you believe the proposed transmission line would have on your property?
A. Based on my observations and understanding as a landowner, I believe the proposed line would substantially
alter the rural character and visual appearance of the area, increase noise levels, and interfere with the peaceful
use and enjoyment of the property. I am also concerned about potential electromagnetic-field exposure and the
possible effects that prolonged exposure may have on nearby residents, children, elderly individuals, persons
with health conditions, livestock, and water resources. While I am not offering expert medical or scientific
testimony, my concerns are informed by publicly available materials and studies discussing such issues. See
Exhibit 6. The projected closeness of the line to my residence and improvements is shown in Exhibit 3.

                              VII. FIRE, STORM, AND SAFETY CONCERNS
Q. Do you have safety concerns related to the proposed route?
A. Yes. Our community recently experienced significant tornado damage and remains in recovery. The area
contains heavy vegetation, dry grass, cedar debris, and other conditions that increase wildfire risk. Based on my
experience living on the property, I am concerned about the possibility of sparks, equipment failures, downed
lines, or other transmission-related events contributing to fire hazards or emergency access issues. The
storm-related materials and photographs are included as Exhibits 4.1 through 4.4, and the wildfire, vegetation,
and firefighter safety materials are included as Exhibits 7.1 through 7.4.

                                      VIII. ROUTING ALTERNATIVES
Q. Are you aware of alternative routes that would reduce impacts?
A. Yes. I believe Route 767 presents a more reasonable alternative because it appears to avoid or reduce
concentrated impacts to residences and community resources when compared to routes utilizing Link F-20.
Based on publicly available routing information, Route 767 also appears to better utilize existing infrastructure
corridors in some areas and would lessen the direct burden placed upon my property and surrounding
landowners. The routing exhibits supporting this comparison are included as Exhibit 2.

                                               IX. CONCLUSION
Q. Please summarize your requested relief.
A. I respectfully request that the Commission reject all proposed routes utilizing Link F-20, including Route 894,
and instead select Route 767 or another route that minimizes impacts to residences, agricultural operations, and
established rural communities.

Written By No765MN

Retired Cardiologist Issues "Black Box Warning" Over Proposed Minnesota
Power Line

ST. PAUL, MN - A retired cardiologist and cardiac electrophysiologist has filed a
formal technical rebuttal with the Minnesota Public Utilities Commission (PUC), issuing
a severe medical warning against the proposed Gopher to Badger Link 765 kV
Transmission Line.

Dr. W. Ben Johnson, a former Institutional Review Board (IRB) chair and Iandowner in
Houston County, claims that the proposed overhead high-voltage lines represent a
